title: Investigate cross-workspace duplication from API key shadow propagation
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported doubled token billing and duplicate ingress counts over short windows after a sequence of proxy redeploys and a downstream claims-merge job. This ticket captures the triage, reproducible test, root-cause hypothesis, and proposed remediation. The behaviour is intermittent and correlated with: (1) ephemeral proxy rotation, (2) concurrent claim-merge window, and (3) service-account delegation events. Initial signs pointed to both attribution duplication and over-counted rate-limiter hits.

Context: Our metering pipeline receives an ingress record when the API gateway accepts a request tagged with an api_key_id and claim_token. Attribution uses a transaction across three systems: gateway (ingress record), claim-service (maps claim_token -> workspace), and billing-aggregator (consumes ingress and emits metering rows). A background job merges duplicate claims for short-lived delegated keys (claim-merge). During claim-merge, some requests' claim_token briefly resolve to the pre-merge and post-merge workspace resulting in two in-flight attribution annotations.

Observed customer impact: Several customers in different orgs saw +95% billing spikes for 3-7 minute windows on 2025-02-12 and 2025-02-14. Rate limiter reported double-consumption for burst windows which caused temporary throttling for a handful of projects. We saw ~1.2k duplicated metering rows across multiple ingestion partitions for each affected minute in the worst case.

Key artifacts: Dashboard: https://console.redwood.example.com/dashboards/billing/duplications (note: internal). Sampling query used to identify duplicates (billing-db): SELECT api_key_id, claim_token, hour_bucket, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM metering.ingress WHERE created_at >= '2025-02-12'::timestamp AND event_name = 'ingress' GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 200;

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally by replaying ingress events while running claim-merge job concurrently; duplication appears when claim-service sometimes returns both old and new workspace ids for claim_token due to eventual-consistency cache TTLs.
- Trace 1 (request-id 59a8c3f2): gateway emitted ingress record, followed by claim-service returning workspace A; claim-merge job replaced mapping to workspace B and re-emitted a sync event that caused the aggregator to accept a second attribution row for the same original request.
- Race window: ~200-800ms depending on Kafka lag and claim-merge batching.
- Root hypothesis: billing-aggregator treats attribution mapping updates as new independent attributions instead of applying an idempotency key tied to request-id + ingress-timestamp. Aggregator consumes both the original attribution and the post-merge reconcile event as distinct meter events.

Reproduction steps (validated in staging):
1) Create ephemeral delegated key and issue a claim_token.
2) Send 100 concurrent requests through gateway with same claim_token.
3) Start claim-merge background job which replaces claim_token->workspace mapping mid-flight.
4) Observe duplicate rows in aggregator and corresponding doubled token counts.

Logs and excerpts:
- Gateway log sample: 2025-02-12T12:04:17Z INFO ingress emitted request_id=59a8c3f2 api_key_id=ak_7Gx... claim_token=ct_3a9
- Claim-service before merge: 2025-02-12T12:04:17Z DEBUG resolve claim_token=ct_3a9 -> workspace=ws_A cache_hit=false
- Claim-merge: 2025-02-12T12:04:17Z INFO merged claim_token ct_3a9: ws_A -> ws_B (seq=342)
- Aggregator consuming re-sync: 2025-02-12T12:04:17Z WARN duplicate attribution detected request_id=59a8c3f2 previous_workspace=ws_A new_workspace=ws_B

Experiments run:
- Applied a quick patch in staging aggregator that checks for existing attribution using (request_id, api_key_id, hour_bucket) idempotency key and rejects second attribution within same 1-minute bucket. Result: duplicate rows reduced by ~98% in staging runs.
- Simulated higher Kafka partition lag: duplication rate increased linearly with lag.

Root cause (final hypothesis): The aggregator currently treats claim re-resolution events as fresh ingress when they are reconciliation events. There is no robust idempotency guard keyed on the original request identifier (gateway request_id) or an ingress-level nonce, and our claim-service does not include the original request_id when emitting a post-merge reconcile event. The combination allows the aggregator to accept two billing-attribution rows for the same logical request.

Decision log:
- Short-term mitigation (accepted): Add a dedupe layer in billing-aggregator that uses idempotency key (request_id + api_key_id + minute_bucket) and an expiration TTL of 24 hours. Implement this as a write-through check against aggregator's local redis cache to avoid cross-node races.
- Long-term fix (accepted): Modify claim-service to include the original ingress request_id in merger re-sync events and change aggregator to treat re-syncs as correction events (update existing attribution row) rather than new events. Also add a transactional reconciliation path where aggregator will attempt to update existing metering row when possible.

Patch references and PRs:
- Staging quickfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-aggregator/pull/1842 (feature/dedupe-idempotency)
- Claim-service follow-up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/claim-service/pull/912 (feature/emit-request-id-on-resync)
- Longer term design doc: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/BILL/Attribution+Reconcile+Design (internal)

Impact and rollout plan:
- Apply short-term dedupe patch to staging and canary (1% traffic) on 2025-03-05. Monitor duplication metrics and downstream billing deltas for 48 hours.
- If stable, ramp to 10% and then 100% over 72 hours.
- Deploy claim-service change in a later release (runtime-1.22.1) with migration window where aggregator accepts request_id-bearing re-syncs as corrections.

Open questions / Risks:
- Dedup TTL: 24 hours is a stopgap; some long-tail incidents could still dedupe incorrectly if legitimate replays occur after TTL expiry. Need to align with replay semantics.
- Memory pressure on local redis caches if high QPS and large idempotency window. Need to add eviction metrics and throttles.
- Potential for partial rollouts causing asymmetric behaviour across nodes (some nodes dedupe, others not) — can cause inconsistent billing until full rollout. Strategy: ensure canary matched by routing policy to avoid splitting customer traffic across mixed behaviour.
steps_to_reproduce: Create an ephemeral delegated api key and claim_token in staging
Issue 100 concurrent generation requests through gateway with the same claim_token
While requests are inflight, trigger claim-service's claim-merge job to replace mapping
Inspect billing-aggregator tables for duplicate attributions by request_id
timeline: 2025-02-12: First customer report of doubled billing spikes; on-call triage started
2025-02-13: Initial reproduction in staging confirmed; quickfix dedupe patch prototyped
2025-02-14: Additional customer spikes correlated with cluster node proxy restarts
2025-03-04: Decision to implement short-term dedupe and long-term claim-service change
decisions: Implement short-term dedupe in billing-aggregator using idempotency key (request_id + api_key_id + minute_bucket)
Modify claim-service to include original request_id on claim-resync events
Treat resync events as corrections (update) rather than new ingestion records in aggregator
next_steps: Merge and deploy aggregator dedupe quickfix to canary on 2025-03-05 (PR #1842)
Run expanded staging load test with injected claim-merge windows to validate dedupe under lag
Implement request_id payload in claim-service PR #912 and run compatibility tests
Add observability: duplication-rate chart, dedupe-hit counters, redis-evictions metric
Schedule post-mortem session with SRE, Billing, and Claim-service owners after full rollout
